content.summary: Welcome to Unit 8. In this reading module, you will explore how journalists and witnesses report what people said during criminal investigations. You will learn the mechanics of shifting verb tenses, pronouns, and time expressions when changing direct speech into reported speech, and you will practice identifying key details in authentic crime reports.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Backshifting tenses in reported statements, questions, and commands.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Specific crime vocabulary including burglars, muggers, shoplifters, and financial penalties.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning for specific witness statements and skimming news reports for main ideas.

learningObjectives: Understand the main arguments and sequences of events in B2 crime reports.
Locate specific details regarding who committed a crime and what witnesses stated.
Recognize and apply correct tense transformations in reported speech structures.

contextWarmup.prompt: When you read a news story about an investigation, what is the most important element to look for first?
options: The exact words and statements given by witnesses and suspects
The personal opinions of the newspaper editor
The advertisements printed next to the article
contextWarmup.explanation: Witness and suspect statements provide the core factual evidence and narrative framework of any crime report.

rules: Present Simple changes to Past Simple: She said, 'I steal cars' becomes She said she stole cars.
Present Continuous changes to Past Continuous: He said, 'I am watching' becomes He said he was watching.
Will changes to would, and can changes to could in reported statements.

commonTrap.explanation: When reporting questions, learners often keep the auxiliary verb structure of direct questions instead of changing to statement word order.
commonTrap.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
commonTrap.correct: He asked me where I lived.

paragraphs: Last Tuesday evening, a daring burglary took place at the municipal museum in central London. According to police reports, a skilled burglar managed to bypass the high-security alarm system and stole several priceless historical artifacts. Chief Inspector Davies stated that they were reviewing security camera footage from neighboring streets to identify the suspect.

An eyewitness working nearby told reporters that she had seen a suspicious person lingering near the back entrance around midnight. She explained that the man was wearing a dark hooded jacket and carrying a heavy canvas bag. Police have asked anyone with additional information about the incident to contact the local station immediately.

connectedSpeech.note: The /t/ sound in what links smoothly to the /h/ sound in happened, often dropping the /h/ entirely in fast speech.
Weak forms cause was to reduce to /wəz/ and blend directly into the surrounding words.
The pronoun us weakens to schwa /əs/ and attaches to the preceding consonant.
Prepositions like to and articles like the reduce significantly in rapid spoken English.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Crime Reports and Reported Statements

content.summary: Master the art of writing formal crime reports and shifting direct speech into accurate reported statements, questions, and commands at the B2 level.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Backshift Tenses in Reported Statements
blueprintItems.example: Detective Miller stated that the suspect had fled the scene.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Converting Direct Questions
blueprintItems.formula: Reporting Verb (asked/inquired) + Question Word / If + Subject + Verb
blueprintItems.example: The officer asked the witness where she had seen the vehicle.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Reporting Imperatives and Requests
blueprintItems.formula: Reporting Verb (ordered/told/asked) + Object + to-infinitive / not to-infinitive
blueprintItems.example: The judge instructed the jury not to discuss the case outside.

mechanicsRules.rule: Omit question marks in reported questions.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The detective asked me where I parked my car?
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The detective asked me where I had parked my car.
mechanicsRules.why: Reported questions are noun clauses functioning as objects, not direct interrogative sentences.

mechanicsRules.rule: Distinguish between 'say' and 'tell' in reported speech.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The witness told that he saw the thief.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The witness said that he had seen the thief.
mechanicsRules.why: 'Tell' requires a direct personal object (told me, told the police), whereas 'say' does not.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize legal terms and official titles correctly.
mechanicsRules.badExample: inspector davis interviewed the suspect at Scotland Yard.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Inspector Davis interviewed the suspect at Scotland Yard.
mechanicsRules.why: Titles combined with proper names and specific headquarters are proper nouns requiring capitalization.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the direct speech into reported speech using a past tense reporting verb:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'I stole the painting from the gallery,' said the thief.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'stole' (Past Simple) to the Past Perfect form 'had stolen'.
targetAnswers: The thief said that he had stolen the painting from the gallery.
The thief said he had stolen the painting from the gallery.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Past simple verbs backshift to the past perfect tense in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the direct question into a reported question:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'Where did you hide the counterfeit money?' the detective asked him.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'asked him where' followed by the subject and the past perfect tense.
targetAnswers: The detective asked him where he had hidden the counterfeit money.
The detective asked him where he had hid the counterfeit money.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order (subject + verb) and omit question marks.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert the direct command into a reported command:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'Don't touch the forensic evidence!' the officer told the civilian.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'told the civilian not to touch' the evidence.
targetAnswers: The officer told the civilian not to touch the forensic evidence.
The officer ordered the civilian not to touch the forensic evidence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Negative imperatives in direct speech change to 'not to' plus the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the grammar, punctuation, and capitalization in this reported statement:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Faulty: the witness told that he saw a masked man running away.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'told that' with 'said that' or 'told the police that'.
targetAnswers: The witness said that he had seen a masked man running away.
The witness stated that he had seen a masked man running away.
The witness said that he saw a masked man running away.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Tell' requires a direct object, whereas 'say' does not take a direct personal object.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the direct speech with modal verbs into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'I can identify the suspect in the lineup,' she stated.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change the modal 'can' to its past form 'could'.
targetAnswers: She stated that she could identify the suspect in the lineup.
She stated she could identify the suspect in the lineup.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The modal verb 'can' changes to 'could' in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert this yes/no direct question into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'Did you witness the robbery on Main Street?' the officer asked her.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'if' or 'whether' after the reporting verb.
targetAnswers: The officer asked her if she had witnessed the robbery on Main Street.
The officer asked her whether she had witnessed the robbery on Main Street.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Yes/no questions in reported speech require 'if' or 'whether' followed by standard word order.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the direct speech statement into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'We are investigating a major cybercrime syndicate,' the chief inspector announced.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'are investigating' (Present Continuous) to 'were investigating'.
targetAnswers: The chief inspector announced that they were investigating a major cybercrime syndicate.
The chief inspector announced that we were investigating a major cybercrime syndicate.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present continuous changes to past continuous in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the punctuation and word order error in this reported question:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Faulty: The judge inquired why did the defendant commit the fraud?
practicumQuestions.hint: Remove the auxiliary 'did', change 'commit' to 'had committed', and remove the question mark.
targetAnswers: The judge inquired why the defendant had committed the fraud.
The judge asked why the defendant had committed the fraud.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Reported questions do not use auxiliary 'do/does/did' and end with a full stop.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the direct speech with 'will' into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'The jury will deliver the verdict tomorrow,' the reporter declared.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change the modal 'will' to 'would'.
targetAnswers: The reporter declared that the jury would deliver the verdict the following day.
The reporter declared that the jury would deliver the verdict tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The future modal 'will' changes to 'would' in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete reported sentence based on this direct quote: 'I have never broken any laws,' insisted the suspect.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct quote: 'I have never broken any laws,' insisted the suspect.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'have never broken' (Present Perfect) to 'had never broken' (Past Perfect).
targetAnswers: The suspect insisted that he had never broken any laws.
The suspect insisted that she had never broken any laws.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present perfect tenses backshift to past perfect in reported speech.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Crime and Reported Speech

content.summary: Mastering spoken reported speech requires clear tense shifting, precise reporting verbs, and natural sentence stress. When you retell what someone else said, you must balance information-carrying words with weak grammatical forms.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on pausing naturally after reporting verbs such as claimed, stated, or explained. Use falling intonation for statements and rising intonation when reporting direct yes-no questions.

pillars.name: Reporting Verb Stress
pillars.target: Emphasize key reporting verbs while reducing pronoun pronouns
pillars.explanation: When saying phrases like 'he told me that', reduce the auxiliary and pronoun sounds to keep the rhythm smooth and conversational.

pillars.name: Backshifting Rhythm
pillars.target: Maintain natural cadence during tense changes
pillars.explanation: Practice moving past tense verbs into past perfect forms without halting your breath flow.

pillars.name: Crime Lexicon Articulation
pillars.target: Clear consonant clusters in legal and criminal vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Words like embezzlement and shoplifter require sharp plosives and distinct syllable boundaries for high clarity.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the primary stress shifts when changing from the noun to the adjective form.
The stress remains on the root syllable in the gerund form.
Compound nouns often stress the first element, while related verbs shift stress depending on context.
The stress stays firmly on the second syllable across both the verb and noun forms.

practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'Where did you hide the counterfeit money?' the detective asked him.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'asked him where' followed by the subject and the past perfect tense.
targetAnswers: The detective asked him where he had hidden the counterfeit money.
The detective asked him where he had hid the counterfeit money.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order (subject + verb) and omit question marks.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert the direct command into a reported command:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'Don't touch the forensic evidence!' the officer told the civilian.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'told the civilian not to touch' the evidence.
targetAnswers: The officer told the civilian not to touch the forensic evidence.
The officer ordered the civilian not to touch the forensic evidence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Negative imperatives in direct speech change to 'not to' plus the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the grammar, punctuation, and capitalization in this reported statement:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Faulty: the witness told that he saw a masked man running away.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'told that' with 'said that' or 'told the police that'.
targetAnswers: The witness said that he had seen a masked man running away.
The witness stated that he had seen a masked man running away.
The witness said that he saw a masked man running away.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Tell' requires a direct object, whereas 'say' does not take a direct personal object.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the direct speech with modal verbs into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'I can identify the suspect in the lineup,' she stated.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change the modal 'can' to its past form 'could'.
targetAnswers: She stated that she could identify the suspect in the lineup.
She stated she could identify the suspect in the lineup.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The modal verb 'can' changes to 'could' in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert this yes/no direct question into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'Did you witness the robbery on Main Street?' the officer asked her.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'if' or 'whether' after the reporting verb.
targetAnswers: The officer asked her if she had witnessed the robbery on Main Street.
The officer asked her whether she had witnessed the robbery on Main Street.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Yes/no questions in reported speech require 'if' or 'whether' followed by standard word order.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the direct speech statement into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'We are investigating a major cybercrime syndicate,' the chief inspector announced.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'are investigating' (Present Continuous) to 'were investigating'.
targetAnswers: The chief inspector announced that they were investigating a major cybercrime syndicate.
The chief inspector announced that we were investigating a major cybercrime syndicate.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present continuous changes to past continuous in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the punctuation and word order error in this reported question:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Faulty: The judge inquired why did the defendant commit the fraud?
practicumQuestions.hint: Remove the auxiliary 'did', change 'commit' to 'had committed', and remove the question mark.
targetAnswers: The judge inquired why the defendant had committed the fraud.
The judge asked why the defendant had committed the fraud.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Reported questions do not use auxiliary 'do/does/did' and end with a full stop.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the direct speech with 'will' into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: 'The jury will deliver the verdict tomorrow,' the reporter declared.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change the modal 'will' to 'would'.
targetAnswers: The reporter declared that the jury would deliver the verdict the following day.
The reporter declared that the jury would deliver the verdict tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The future modal 'will' changes to 'would' in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete reported sentence based on this direct quote: 'I have never broken any laws,' insisted the suspect.

targetAnswers: The suspect insisted that he had never broken any laws.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Present perfect tenses backshift to past perfect in reported speech.
